title: Subarray Squares
explanation: Split into k parts minimizing Σ(part sum)². dp[j][i] with an O(n) min per state is O(k·n²) = 2.7e10. The best split point is monotone in i → divide & conquer DP (or CHT).
traps: Squared part sums get large; use 64-bit integers.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[j][i] = minimum cost to split the first i elements into j subarrays
dp[l][r] = minimum cost to split a[l..r]
options.why: You also need how many parts are used; and O(n³) is too slow.

options.text: dp[i] = minimum cost for the first i elements
options.why: Loses the number of parts used (must be exactly k).

options.text: dp[s] = minimum parts with total square s
options.why: Square sums are huge and that isn't the question.

extraLayers.explanation: Partition into exactly k contiguous groups → (groups used, prefix length).

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[j][i] = min over p < i of dp[j−1][p] + (pre_i − pre_p)²; opt(i) is monotone, so compute each layer with divide & conquer in O(n log n)
Same recurrence with a direct loop over p
Binary search on the maximum part sum
options.why: That solves 'minimize the largest part', a different objective.

extraLayers.explanation: The split point for i+1 is never left of the split point for i, so solve the middle i first and recurse on halves with a narrowed range.
